newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Ringgit turns softer on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Ringgit turns softer on profit-taking.

text.p: The ringgit turned softer in late Asian trading on profit-taking after the local unit had earlier firmed on commercial selling of the dollar, dealers said.
"Selling of the dollar stopped at 2.5040 and players then started to buy back dollar/ringgit," said a dealer with a foreign bank in Kuala Lumpur. "It looks like most of the selling has been done."
The dollar sales had begun on Monday afternoon.
Dealers said there was talk that a Malaysian oil company was looking to sell a large amount of dollars against the ringgit.
A decline in the dollar/majors had also aided the ringgit's rise earlier, dealers said.
Dealers said there was strong support for the dollar at 2.5030, adding that the ringgit's topside is likely to be capped at 2.5000 a dollar.
They said they expected the ringgit to remain rangebound due to lack of fresh factors.
At 1000 GMT, the ringgit was at 2.5073/80 a dollar against 2.5058/68 at close of Kuala Lumpur on Monday.
